Assist the thespian in a performance to gain his services in your adventures.

==Quest information==

===Requirements===
*Having chosen [[Goren]] to accompany [[Midauha]] in Istan in the quest [[Brains or Brawn]].
{{Standard prerequisites
 |campaign = Nightfall
 |nationality = all
 |unstarted = [[Gain Norgu]]
}}

===Objectives===
*Perform with [[Norgu]] in [[Jahinur]].
*Write a short script with Norgu.
*Perform with Norgu in [[Pojah Estates]].
*Protect Norgu from the dangers of [[Vehtendi Valley]].
*Destroy the [[heket]] that have overrun the performance area.
*Register Norgu's play rights with [[Records Keeper Palin]] at the Writing Guild of Vabbi.

===Reward===
*2,000 [[Experience]]
*[[Norgu]] joins your party.

==Walkthrough==
The initial quest objective can be approached from either [[Honur Hill]] or [[the Kodash Bazaar]].  Going from Honur Hill will take you through [[Yahnur Market]], and while this isn't an often frequented outpost, it may be worth seeing on your way through for exploration purposes. Going from the Kodash Bazaar may be easier.

===From Honur Hill===
From Honur Hill, head due south along the west side of Resplendent Makuun to arrive at Yahnur Market, then on into [[Vehtendi Valley]].  Although the first objective is due west of Yahnur Market, it will be necessary to take a route that turns south, west over the fields, then north to meet with Norgu. This area mainly has Heket, Behemoths and Kournans. The Behemoth Gravebanes act as [[minion master]]s and also inflict degeneration using hexes on the party, so kill them first if possible.

===From Kodash Bazaar===
Very simply, head due south from the bazaar, you will most likely encounter Kournans and some plant [[mob]]s along the way.

===The Meeting===
On meeting Norgu at [[Jahinur]] (point 1 on the map), you'll get the chance to create a script via some multiple choice dialogue, then watch the audience response to his "masterpiece". After the first performance at Jahinur, you must escort Norgu north to his next engagement (at point 2), making sure he doesn't die on the way.  As a level 18 mesmer, Norgu provides some assistance, casting [[Clumsiness]], [[Mantra of Persistence]], and [[Conjure Phantasm]] as required.

Once the last objective is activated, it's an easy matter of [[map travel]]ing to the Kodash Bazaar and collecting your reward and a new mesmer hero.

===Reward dialogue===
'''Records Keeper Palin'''
:''"Another play from Norgu?  You don't want to know how his last one played out, believe me.  Well if you want to sell the rights to your story, that's your business.  But you should ask Norgu about his other play, "The Epic Tale of the Brave Lanterns: Part One.""''

==Notes==
*On your way from the first play to the next engagement with the heket, the quest [[The Hanging Gardener]] can be picked up and completed soon after this quest is finished (see point 3 on the maps above).
*If you are not in a hurry to acquire Norgu, it is easier to complete [[Gain Norgu]] than this quest, since that quest only requires you to speak to [[Korvus]]. The Gain Norgu quest also awards 500 more experience than this quest.

==Trivia==
*The Latin phrase "magnum opus" literally translates to "great work," and is used to describe a dramatist's masterpiece.  Norgu's phrase "opus maximus" literally translates to "greatest work," perhaps indicating that his work surpasses the ordinary masterpiece.
*Brave Lantern is possibly a reference to the [[w:The Brave Little Toaster|The Brave Little Toaster]].
*The "lich lord" and "smote the evil atop a volcano" script options are likely references to the plotline of Guild Wars Prophecies.
*The forgotten, dark god script option is likely a reference to the plotline of Nightfall.
*The disgruntled piemaster script option may be a reference to [[w:List of Strawberry Shortcake villains#The Peculiar Purple Pieman of Porcupine Peak|The Peculiar Purple Pieman of Porcupine Peak]], a [[w:Strawberry Shortcake|Strawberry Shortcake]] villain, or [[w:Mrs. Lovett|Mrs. Lovett]], the accomplice of [[w:Sweeney Todd|Sweeney Todd]]'s title character.
*"Brave, brave, BRAVE <hero> may be a reference to the song of Sir Robin's minstrel in [[w:Monty Python and the Holy Grail|Monty Python and the Holy Grail]].
